clue.text: Buffet near main part of London

parts.note: to buffet is to batter, strike repeatedly
the main is a poetic word for the sea

explanation.surface: A self-service meal laid on near the heart of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a meal but is a verb; 'main' looks like 'principal' but is the sea. BATTERSEA is a district of south London on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is a district on the south bank of the Thames, home to the famous power station.

clue.text: Stops buffs heading off in pursuit of Australian book

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to buff is to polish, so buffs means polishes

explanation.surface: Someone stops shining things up to chase after an Australian book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pursuit of' puts the trimmed POLISHES after A and B.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish something is to put an end to it, so abolishes is a synonym of stops.

clue.text: Double smallest amount of electricity in coil

parts.note: a double is a twin, an exact counterpart

indicators.note: the smallest amount of a word is its first letter alone

explanation.surface: A faint electrical charge doubled up inside a wound coil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' looks like a verb but is the noun TWIN; 'in' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Twine as a verb means to wind or twist round, which is what coiling is.

clue.text: I could be the merry sonnet's source

definitions.text: I could be the merry sonnet's source

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may become something else when reordered
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A jolly poem's author introduces himself as the origin of the verse.
explanation.walkthrough: THEMERRY plus S is rearranged; read whole, the clue describes the answer, a writer of verse who could produce a merry sonnet.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a writer of light or mediocre verse, a plausible author of a cheerful sonnet.

clue.text: After Henry goes, raises part of roof

indicators.note: goes says the letter departs from the word

parts.note: heaves means lifts or raises with effort
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Once Henry has left, someone hoists up a section of the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is a link: HEAVES with its H gone leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The eaves are the overhanging lower edges of a roof, a part of the roof structure.

clue.text: Firm happy to manipulate accounts, say

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
OK means content or happy with something

explanation.surface: A business is quite content to fiddle its books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that accounts are just one example of what can be falsified.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook the books is an idiom for falsifying financial records, so cook means to doctor them.

clue.text: Head on and on, covering Italy

indicators.note: covering says the two words surround the letter for Italy

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A headline that runs on and on, all about Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The two ONs sit either side of I.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses onion for the human head, as in being off one's onion.

clue.text: King, with plea for help about rise of offspring, ruined city

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: in a down clue the rise of a word is that word read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a son is offspring
SOS is the distress signal, a plea for help

explanation.surface: A king calls for help over his son's rebellion in a city now in ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: NOS is SON read upwards; the palindrome SOS reads the same whichever way it goes, so 'about' changes nothing. KNOSSOS is the ruined Minoan palace-city on Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: Knossos is the Bronze Age Cretan site, now in ruins, linked with King Minos and the Minotaur.

clue.text: Metal shard I moved higher

indicators.note: in a down entry higher means nearer the top, so the letter shifts towards the start

parts.note: a sliver is a thin splinter or shard

explanation.surface: A splinter of metal I shifted further up.
explanation.walkthrough: In SLIVER the I climbs one place above the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is a precious metallic element, symbol Ag.

clue.text: Lake in Germany ridiculed — provided tiny amount of water

parts.note: D is the vehicle code for Germany, from Deutschland

indicators.note: in puts the letter for lake inside the other pieces

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease or ridicule them

explanation.surface: A German lake is mocked for supplying only a trickle of water.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes into DRIBBED, after the B pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To dribble is to let liquid fall in small drops, giving only a trickle.

clue.text: Change size of study that's risky, losing repeated item, after one takes the lead

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: losing repeated item says one copy of the doubled letter is dropped

parts.note: iffy means doubtful or risky

explanation.surface: A dicey study being slimmed down once someone takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing repeated item' drops one of the doubled letters; 'after one takes the lead' means the numeral goes in front. 'Change size of' is fair because iconifying shrinks a window.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, to iconify a window is to shrink it to an icon, changing its size on screen.

clue.text: Hitchcock film extremely cut? Time I quit

indicators.note: cut means the word is trimmed of its final letter

parts.note: very means extremely
to go is to leave or quit

explanation.surface: Was a Hitchcock film heavily edited, so it's time I walked out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely cut' looks like heavy editing; it is VERY docked to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is Alfred Hitchcock's 1958 thriller starring James Stewart.

clue.text: Silent river creatures start to struggle around wintry weather

indicators.note: around says the animals are wrapped about the frozen weather

parts.note: water voles live along riverbanks
ice is wintry weather

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Riverbank animals, mute, begin to struggle in icy conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river' tempts you to write R, but 'river creatures' together are the water-dwelling rodents; 'around' wraps them about the frozen weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Voiceless means lacking a voice, making no sound, so it is a synonym of silent.

clue.text: Remains single, investing in building society

indicators.note: investing in suggests putting something inside, so the number goes into the abbreviation

parts.note: BS is an abbreviation for building society, a British savings and mortgage institution
single means one

explanation.surface: A lone saver keeps putting money into a building society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb but is the noun. A building society is a British mutual savings and mortgage lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Bones are what is left of a body after death, its mortal remains.

clue.text: That chap in pub rejected treatment for alcoholism?

indicators.note: rejected suggests something thrown back, so the letters are read in reverse
in places the pronoun inside the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
he refers to that chap

explanation.surface: A man turned away from the pub: is he going in for drying out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' makes BAHER and 'rejected' reads it backwards; the question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab, short for rehabilitation, is the programme used to treat addiction, alcoholism included.

clue.text: Hippo, perhaps, with its head beset by insects

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the letter goes inside the insects

parts.note: a bee and a moth are insects
its refers back to Hippo, whose head is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hippo's head plagued by swarming insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its head' takes the first letter of Hippo, the definition word, and 'beset by' puts it among the two insects. 'perhaps' marks the hippo as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A behemoth is any enormous creature; the biblical Behemoth is often identified with the hippopotamus.

clue.text: Sources of wood used around part of window frame recalled garden items

indicators.note: used around says the trees wrap the reversed frame part

parts.note: trees are where wood comes from

indicators.note: recalled suggests calling back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the sill is the bottom part of a window frame

explanation.surface: Timber surrounding a window remembered as part of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' gives LLIS and 'used around' sets the trees about it. 'Sources of wood' looks like a first-letters signal but is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Trellises are lattice frameworks put up in gardens to support climbing plants.

clue.text: Appearing placid is good in unusually noisy age

indicators.note: in puts the letter for good inside the rearranged letters
unusually suggests the letters arranged in an uncommon way

explanation.surface: Seeming calm counts for a lot in an unusually loud era.
explanation.walkthrough: NOISYAGE is rearranged as EASYOING and G goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-going describes a relaxed, calm temperament, so someone seeming placid fits.

clue.text: Author still succeeded working after getting stone on head

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
even can mean still, as in even better
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: An author keeps going after being struck on the head by a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after getting stone on head' puts ST at the top of the down entry. Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was the Scottish writer of Treasure Island and Kidnapped.

clue.text: British sailor heading for port — hours at sea crossing from Europe to Asia

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: the heading for a word is its first letter
at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A British sailor makes for port, spending hours at sea crossing between continents.
explanation.walkthrough: HOURS rearranged gives HORUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bosphorus is the strait at Istanbul separating European and Asian Turkey, where ships cross between the continents.

clue.text: Unfair offer securing most of a good thing

indicators.note: securing means holding, so the offer is placed around the rest

parts.note: a bid is an offer

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: an asset is a useful or good thing

explanation.surface: A one-sided offer that locks in most of the benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' docks the last letter to leave ASSE, and 'securing' has the offer hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: Biased means prejudiced or unfair, favouring one side.

clue.text: Aspiration concerning blocking engineering project?

indicators.note: blocking says the short word sits inside and blocks the other

parts.note: a dam is a major engineering project
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An ambition stands in the way of a big civil engineering scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' is apt, since a dam blocks water and here something blocks the dam.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a cherished hope or ambition, which is what an aspiration is.

clue.text: Damage concealment I abandoned in wonder

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: abandoned says the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a veil is a means of concealment

explanation.surface: Someone damages their cover, which they gave up in astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: VEIL without its I is VEL; 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel is something astonishing, a wonder.

clue.text: How the Marines panic?

parts.note: a la means in the manner of, so how something is done
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A question about the way the Marines lose their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: A LA RM reads as in the style of the Royal Marines.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or anxiety, which is what panic is.

clue.text: Pointer to dispute undermining Arabia

indicators.note: in a down clue undermining puts one piece below the other

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A sign of a quarrel that is weakening Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undermining' only works in a down entry, where one piece is literally placed below the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a sign used to point the way, a pointer.

clue.text: Half of Belgians are shocked by Queen — drinking this?

definitions.text: Half of Belgians are shocked by Queen — drinking this?

indicators.note: shocked suggests letters jolted out of order
half of a word is its first half, here four letters of eight

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Many Belgians are scandalised to see the Queen drinking beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocked' rearranges the half-word and ARE into LAGERBE; the whole clue then pictures what the Queen is drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager beer is a light beer, plausibly what the shocking royal is sipping.

clue.text: Left husband, leaving the dull hunk in uncertain state

indicators.note: leaving says the letter departs from the word

parts.note: a himbo is a handsome but dim man

explanation.surface: A wife walks out on her husband, quitting the handsome dimwit, unsure what next.
explanation.walkthrough: HIMBO, the male counterpart of bimbo, loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in limbo means being in an undecided, uncertain intermediate state.

clue.text: Fake American politician runs over

parts.note: a Rep is a Representative in the US Congress
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A phoney US politician turns tail and runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs over' looks like a phrase but gives R and O separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A repro is a reproduction, a copy passed off as or mistaken for the original.

clue.text: Class in area of study backed by corporation

indicators.note: backed suggests turning back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: the arts are an area of study
corporation is old slang for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A lesson in some field of learning sponsored by a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company; it is jokey slang for a pot belly, a TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer of society, a social class or level.

clue.text: Drive finishing early, blocked by one stupid dead end

indicators.note: blocked by says the trimmed verb has something stuck inside it
finishing early says the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: to impel is to drive forward
an ass is a stupid person

explanation.surface: A drive cut short by a fool ends up going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' leaves IMPE and 'blocked by' plugs it; 'one stupid' is a single noun phrase, not the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation with no way forward, a deadlock or dead end.

clue.text: Beginning with name when meeting US lawyer

indicators.note: when meeting says the pieces join up side by side

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, a US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: Starting out with a name to meet an American attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: The lawyer comes first, then W and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the start of the day, and figuratively the beginning of anything.

clue.text: Pine toilets: they're warm in winter

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it
john is US slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Pine-panelled lavatories that stay cosy through winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the timber but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Long johns are full-length thermal underwear worn to keep warm in cold weather.
